summary: Two Python services on EKS with zero-code OpenTelemetry: orders calls inventory over HTTP with a 500 ms timeout, inventory has 4 worker threads at 40 ms a request. An open-loop load of 40 orders a second runs 110 s per run, and at second 20 inventory slows to 2 s a request for 20 s. Six runs alternate with fresh pods and their own order numbers: naive (instant retries, up to 3 more) and budget (exponential backoff with full jitter and a 10% retry budget, credited together), three of each. analyze.sh counts, for the 70 s after the slowdown: failed orders, recovery to 95% success and how fast, calls per order, failed calls by kind (timeout, refused or reset), retries the budget skipped, the share of inventory's work started after the caller's timeout (X-Caller-Deadline header), inventory's queue of requests waiting for a thread, latency before and after with n, and CPU of both containers (average and busiest second) plus the node's busiest second. Inventory logs the server settings it really started with. fix.sh reads the naive-2 and budget-2 windows back from Splunk Observability Cloud (request counts and 503s from the services' OpenTelemetry HTTP server metric, per route) until two reads agree, checks Splunk's orders count against the load's count (inventory's comparison printed too), and prints the Splunk APM service map. Splunk also gives the storm itself: orders' HTTP client metric counts every call to inventory, timeouts included, so calls per order is read from Splunk next to the lab's own count.
expected: reproduce.sh runs naive-1, budget-1 and naive-2; each starts healthy (at least 95% success before the slowdown) and loses orders during it; naive-1 shows failed orders after the slowdown; then HERO_RESULT: reproduced. fix.sh runs budget-2, naive-3 and budget-3 the same way; all three budget runs recover to 95% within 70 s, Splunk returns the budget-2 window, then HERO_RESULT: fixed. Whether naive runs recover is the measured result, not a condition.

# Retry storm after a slowdown, seen in Splunk APM

Two Python services on EKS: `orders` takes an order and calls `inventory` over HTTP with a 500 ms timeout. Both run with
zero-code OpenTelemetry (`opentelemetry-instrument`) and send traces to the Splunk OTel Collector. `inventory` has 4 worker
threads and takes 40 ms a request, so it can finish about 100 a second.

An open-loop load sends 40 orders a second for 110 s. At second 20 it asks inventory for a 20 s slowdown: every request takes
2 s. After that inventory is healthy again. Each run gets fresh pods and its own order numbers. Runs alternate, three of each
mode: naive-1, budget-1 and naive-2 in `reproduce.sh`, budget-2, naive-3 and budget-3 in `fix.sh`.

| Run | Retry setting in `orders` |
| --- | --- |
| `naive` | retry a failed call at once, up to 3 more times |
| `budget` | retry up to 3 more times with exponential backoff and full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 2 s), only while a retry budget allows: each order adds 0.1 of a retry |

`analyze.sh` reads the load output, the orders log and the inventory log for each run and prints, for the 70 s after the
slowdown ended: failed orders, whether and when success got back to 95% for 5 s in a row, inventory calls per order,
retries the budget skipped, latency of successful orders, and how many requests inventory started after the caller's timeout
had already passed (orders sends its deadline in an `X-Caller-Deadline` header), with each container's CPU from its cgroup (average and busiest second), the node's busiest second from /proc/stat,
inventory's queue of accepted requests waiting for a thread, failed calls by kind (timeout, refused or reset, HTTP), and the
server settings inventory actually started with.
`fix.sh` then reads the naive-2 and budget-2 windows back from Splunk Observability Cloud: request counts and 503s from
the stable HTTP server metric the services send (`http.server.request.duration_count`, filtered to each route), until two reads agree, and checks Splunk's orders count against the requests orders logged as finished in the same window (both count a request
when the server finishes it; when orders falls behind in the instant-retry runs, it finishes fewer than the load sends). It also reads orders' HTTP client metric (`http.client.request.duration_count`, server.address inventory), which counts every call
orders made to inventory, timeouts included, and divides by the order requests: the retry storm's calls per order, in Splunk.
Inventory's counts are compared and printed too, but its rate changes fast after
the slowdown, so they aren't the check.
The `budget` mode changes three things at once (backoff, jitter, budget), so the post credits the combination, not one part.

- `check.sh`: the free check, the same two runs in Docker with an OTLP sink instead of Splunk.
- `lib.sh`: the clock, starting a run, the load and the report. `splunk.sh`: the Splunk reads.

The slowdown is simulated, and this is one load level, one timeout and one dependency. The backlog of requests clients
already gave up on still has to drain; server-side load shedding isn't tested here.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reads one run's three logs and prints the counts, raw first, then HERO_MEASURE lines. Code only, no model.
# Usage: bash analyze.sh <run label> <load output> <orders log> <inventory log>
exec python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
import sys, re
label, load_f, orders_f, inv_f = sys.argv[1:5]
WINDOW, CONTROL = 70, 20
text = open(load_f).read()
st = re.search(r"LOAD start=(\d+) rate=(\d+)", text); start, rate = int(st[1]), int(st[2])
sl = re.search(r"SLOWDOWN start=(\d+) end=(\d+) second=(\d+) seconds=(\d+)", text)
slow_at, slow_s = int(sl[3]), int(sl[4]); end_s = slow_at + slow_s
per = {int(m[1]): (int(m[2]), int(m[3])) for m in re.finditer(r"LOAD second=(\d+) ok=(\d+) failed=(\d+)", text)}
sent = int(re.search(r"LOAD end=\d+ sent=(\d+)", text)[1])
total = lambda rows: (sum(o for o, f in rows), sum(f for o, f in rows))
b_ok, b_fail = total([per.get(s, (0, 0)) for s in range(slow_at - CONTROL, slow_at)])
d_ok, d_fail = total([per.get(s, (0, 0)) for s in range(slow_at, end_s)])
after = [(s, *per.get(s, (0, 0))) for s in range(end_s, end_s + WINDOW)]
a_ok, a_fail = sum(x[1] for x in after), sum(x[2] for x in after)
rec = next((after[i][0] - end_s for i in range(len(after) - 4)
            if all(after[j][1] + after[j][2] > 0 and after[j][1] / (after[j][1] + after[j][2]) >= 0.95 for j in range(i, i + 5))), None)
w0, w1 = start + end_s, start + end_s + WINDOW
rows = [tuple(map(int, m.groups())) for m in re.finditer(r"ORDER \d+ ok=(\d) attempts=(\d+) denied=(\d) ms=(\d+) t=(\d+)", open(orders_f).read())]
win = [r for r in rows if w0 <= r[4] < w1]
calls, denied = sum(r[1] for r in win), sum(r[2] for r in win)
cpo = calls / len(win) if win else 0
lat = sorted(r[3] for r in win if r[0] == 1)
pre = sorted(r[3] for r in rows if r[0] == 1 and start + slow_at - CONTROL <= r[4] < start + slow_at)
pq = lambda xs, q: xs[min(len(xs) - 1, int(q * len(xs)))] if xs else None
p = lambda q: pq(lat, q)
inv = [tuple(m.groups()) for m in re.finditer(r"INVENTORY t=(\d+) handled=(\d+) late=(\d+) queued=(-?\d+) cpu_usec=(\S+) node_busy=(\d+) node_total=(\d+)", open(inv_f).read())]
iw = [r for r in inv if w0 <= int(r[0]) < w1]
handled, late = sum(int(r[1]) for r in iw), sum(int(r[2]) for r in iw)
def cores_of(samples):   # (t, usec) pairs inside the window -> average cores used
    s = [(int(t), int(u)) for t, u in samples if u.isdigit()]
    return (s[-1][1] - s[0][1]) / 1e6 / (s[-1][0] - s[0][0]) if len(s) > 1 and s[-1][0] > s[0][0] else None
def peak_of(samples):    # (t, usec) pairs -> the busiest single second, in cores
    s = [(int(t), int(u)) for t, u in samples if u.isdigit()]
    return max(((b[1] - a[1]) / 1e6 / (b[0] - a[0]) for a, b in zip(s, s[1:]) if b[0] > a[0]), default=None)
otext = open(orders_f).read()
orows = [m.groups() for m in re.finditer(r"ORDERS t=(\d+) cpu_usec=(\S+) timeouts=(\d+) conn_errors=(\d+) http_errors=(\d+)", otext) if w0 <= int(m[1]) < w1]
cores, ocores = cores_of((r[0], r[4]) for r in iw), cores_of((r[0], r[1]) for r in orows)
ipeak, opeak = peak_of((r[0], r[4]) for r in iw), peak_of((r[0], r[1]) for r in orows)
nodes = [(int(r[5]), int(r[6])) for r in iw]
npeak = max(((b[0] - a[0]) / (b[1] - a[1]) for a, b in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]) if b[1] > a[1]), default=None)   # busy share of the node
qpeak = max((int(r[3]) for r in iw), default=None)
timeouts, conns, https = (sum(int(r[k]) for r in orows) for k in (2, 3, 4))
srv = re.search(r"INVENTORY server threads=(\d+) backlog=(\d+) connection_limit=(\d+)", open(inv_f).read())
late_pct = 100 * late / handled if handled else 0
fmt = lambda c: f"{c:.2f}" if c is not None else "null"
print(f"{label}: success per 10 s after the slowdown (ok/sent): " + " ".join(f"{sum(x[1] for x in after[i:i+10])}/{sum(x[1]+x[2] for x in after[i:i+10])}" for i in range(0, WINDOW, 10)))
print(f"{label}: before {b_ok}/{b_ok + b_fail} ok; during {d_fail}/{d_ok + d_fail} failed; after {a_fail}/{a_ok + a_fail} failed; back to 95% for 5 s: " + (f"{rec} s" if rec is not None else f"not within {WINDOW} s"))
print(f"{label}: orders log: {len(win)} orders, {calls} calls ({cpo:.2f} per order), retries skipped by budget {denied}; failed calls: timeouts {timeouts}, refused or reset {conns}, HTTP {https}")
print(f"{label}: latency ms p50/p99 (n): before {pq(pre, 0.5)}/{pq(pre, 0.99)} ({len(pre)}), after {p(0.5)}/{p(0.99)} ({len(lat)})")
print(f"{label}: inventory finished {handled} ({handled / max(1, len(iw)):.1f}/s), {late} started after the caller's timeout ({late_pct:.1f}%), queue peak {qpeak}; " + (f"{srv[1]} threads, backlog {srv[2]}, limit {srv[3]}" if srv else "server line missing"))
print(f"{label}: CPU cores avg/peak: inventory {fmt(cores)}/{fmt(ipeak)}, orders {fmt(ocores)}/{fmt(opeak)}; node peak {fmt(npeak * 100 if npeak is not None else None)}%")
pct = lambda a, b: f"{100 * a / b:.1f}" if b else "null"
mode = label.split("-")[0]
nz = lambda v: "null" if v is None else v
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: orders_success_before_pct[{label}]={pct(b_ok, b_ok + b_fail)}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: failed_orders_during_slowdown[{label}]={d_fail}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: failed_orders_after_slowdown[{label}]={a_fail}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: recovery_after_slowdown[{label}/recovered]={1 if rec is not None else 0}")
if rec is not None:
    print(f"HERO_MEASURE: recovery_after_slowdown[{label}/seconds]={rec}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: calls_after_slowdown[{label}/calls-per-order]={cpo:.2f}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: calls_after_slowdown[{label}/timeouts]={timeouts}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: calls_after_slowdown[{label}/refused-or-reset]={conns}")
if mode == "budget":
    print(f"HERO_MEASURE: calls_after_slowdown[{label}/retries-skipped-by-budget]={denied}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: inventory_late_share_after[{label}]={late_pct:.1f}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: inventory_queue_peak_after[{label}]={nz(qpeak)}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: order_latency_ms[{label}/before-p50]={nz(pq(pre, 0.5))}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: order_latency_ms[{label}/before-p99]={nz(pq(pre, 0.99))}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: order_latency_ms[{label}/after-p50]={nz(p(0.5))}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: order_latency_ms[{label}/after-p99]={nz(p(0.99))}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: cpu_cores_after[{label}/inventory-avg]={fmt(cores)}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: cpu_cores_after[{label}/inventory-peak]={fmt(ipeak)}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: cpu_cores_after[{label}/orders-avg]={fmt(ocores)}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: cpu_cores_after[{label}/orders-peak]={fmt(opeak)}")
print(f"HERO_MEASURE: cpu_cores_after[{label}/node-peak-pct]={fmt(npeak * 100 if npeak is not None else None)}")
# The same window on 10-second boundaries, which is how Splunk APM buckets its counts, with the logs' counts inside it.
a0, a1 = -(-w0 // 10) * 10, w1 // 10 * 10
sent_a = sum(sum(per.get(s - start, (0, 0))) for s in range(a0, a1))
handled_a = sum(int(r[1]) for r in inv if a0 <= int(r[0]) < a1)
done_a = [r for r in rows if a0 <= r[4] < a1]   # orders that orders itself finished in the window, by its own log, and the calls they made
print(f"WINDOW {label} {a0} {a1} {sent_a} {handled_a} {1 if rec is not None else 0} {len(done_a)} {sum(r[1] for r in done_a)}   (10 s boundaries: start, end, orders sent, inventory finished, recovered, orders finished, their inventory calls)")
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, on a GitHub runner with Docker, before AWS is paid for. It runs the lab's real code (the same files the
# manifests carry) in python:3.12-slim with the pinned packages and zero-code OpenTelemetry, both retry modes, with the
# same load and slowdown. Kubernetes and Splunk are not tested here. The naive result is printed, not asserted: that is
# the lab's finding. The budget run must recover, because that is the fix the article shows.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
mkdir -p c/app c/load c/venv

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
for k in ("requirements.txt", "inventory.py", "orders.py"):
    open(f"c/app/{k}", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", k))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
PY
IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ "]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== One virtualenv with the pinned packages, as the build Job makes it"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/app:/app:ro" -v "$PWD/c/venv:/lab/venv" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  python -m venv /lab/venv && /lab/venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir -r /app/requirements.txt &&
  /lab/venv/bin/pip freeze | grep -iE "^(flask|waitress|requests|opentelemetry-(distro|sdk|instrumentation-flask|instrumentation-requests))=="'

# A tiny OTLP sink stands in for the Collector: it answers 200 and counts the trace exports it receives.
cat > c/sink.py <<'PY'
import http.server, threading
n = {"posts": 0}
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))); n["posts"] += 1
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Length", "0"); self.end_headers()
    def do_GET(self):
        b = str(n["posts"]).encode(); self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b)
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 4318), H).serve_forever()
PY
OTEL="-e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://sink:4318 -e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf -e OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp -e OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL=10000 -e OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=http -e OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none -e PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1"
start() {   # service, extra env...
  local s=$1; shift
  docker rm -f "$s" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run -d --name "$s" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/app:/lab/app:ro" -v "$PWD/c/venv:/lab/venv:ro" $OTEL -e "OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=$s" "$@" \
    "$IMAGE" /lab/venv/bin/opentelemetry-instrument /lab/venv/bin/python "/lab/app/$s.py" >/dev/null
}
ready() {   # service, port
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do docker exec "$1" /lab/venv/bin/python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:$2/healthz', timeout=2)" 2>/dev/null && return 0; sleep 1; done
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: $1 didn't start"; exit 1
}

run() {   # run label (naive-1, budget-1), first order
  echo "== $1"
  docker rm -f sink >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run -d --name sink --network lab -v "$PWD/c/sink.py:/sink.py:ro" "$IMAGE" python /sink.py >/dev/null
  start inventory -e THREADS=4 -e WORK_MS=40
  start orders -e THREADS=400 -e INVENTORY_URL=http://inventory:8081 -e "RETRY_MODE=${1%-*}"
  ready inventory 8081; ready orders 8080
  docker run --rm --name load --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e RATE=40 -e LOAD_SECONDS=110 -e "FIRST=$2" \
    -e ORDERS_HOST=orders -e INVENTORY_HOST=inventory -e SLOW_AT=20 -e SLOW_SECONDS=20 -e SLOW_MS=2000 "$IMAGE" python /load/load.py > "c/load-$1.txt"
  docker logs orders > "c/orders-$1.log" 2>&1
  docker logs inventory > "c/inventory-$1.log" 2>&1
  sleep 6   # one more export interval
  posts=$(docker exec sink python -c "import urllib.request; print(urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:4318/').read().decode())")
  echo "$1: OTLP exports (traces and metrics) the sink received from both services: $posts"
  [ "${posts:-0}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: zero-code OpenTelemetry exported nothing"; exit 1; }
  docker rm -f orders inventory sink >/dev/null
  bash analyze.sh "$1" "c/load-$1.txt" "c/orders-$1.log" "c/inventory-$1.log" | tee "c/report-$1.txt"
  grep -q "orders_success_before_pct\[$1\]=\(9[5-9]\|100\)" "c/report-$1.txt" || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the $1 run started unhealthy"; exit 1; }
}

run naive-1 1
run budget-1 10001
grep -q 'recovery_after_slowdown\[budget-1/recovered\]=1' c/report-budget-1.txt || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the budget run didn't recover within 70 s"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'failed_orders_after_slowdown\[naive-1\]=[1-9]' c/report-naive-1.txt || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the naive run had no failures after the slowdown, so there is nothing to show"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'inventory_late_share_after\[naive-1\]=' c/report-naive-1.txt || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the late-work count is missing"; exit 1; }
echo "CHECK PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BUILD: RETRY_MODE=budget, the combination this post credits as one fix: exponential backoff with full jitter (base 100 ms,
# cap 2 s) and a retry budget (each order adds 0.1 of a retry, so retries stay near 10% of calls). Same code, image, load
# and slowdown. Runs budget-2, naive-3 and budget-3 (reproduce.sh ran naive-1, budget-1, naive-2), then reads the naive-2 and budget-2 windows
# back from Splunk APM and compares them with the lab's own logs.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
. ./splunk.sh

start_clock 830 not_fixed

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
for v in SPLUNK_REALM SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN SPLUNK_API_TOKEN; do [ -n "${!v:-}" ] || fail "$v is not set"; done
LOAD_NODE=$(cat load-node.txt) || fail "no load node recorded"

echo "== 1. The before-check: the cluster's own data reaches Splunk"
wait_cluster "$(cap 90 700)"
echo "cluster metric time series in Splunk: ${cluster:-0}"
[ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no cluster data reached Splunk, so a zero here would prove nothing"

n=2
for run in budget-2 naive-3 budget-3; do
  echo "== $n. Run $run"
  start_run "$run" 100
  load_run "$run" "$(cap 200 120)"
  report "$run"
  n=$(( n + 1 ))
done

echo "== $n. The naive-2 and budget-2 windows in Splunk Observability Cloud, next to the lab's own counts"
for run in naive-2 budget-2; do
  read a0 a1 sent handled _ ofin ocalls _ < "window-$run.txt" || fail "no window recorded for $run"
  stable_count orders all "$a0" "$a1"; total=$count
  stable_count orders true "$a0" "$a1"; errors=$count
  stable_count inventory all "$a0" "$a1"; inv=$count
  stable_count orders client "$a0" "$a1"; calls=$count
  echo "$run, seconds $a0 to $a1: Splunk orders requests $total (errors $errors), orders finished by its own log $ofin (load sent $sent); Splunk inventory requests $inv, lab inventory finished $handled; Splunk calls to inventory $calls, orders log $ocalls"
  pct=$(awk -v e="$errors" -v t="$total" 'BEGIN { if (t > 0) printf "%.1f", 100 * e / t; else print "null" }')
  # The check: Splunk's orders count against the requests orders itself logged as finished in the same window (both count a
  # request when the server finishes it). The load's sent count is printed too: when orders falls behind, it finishes fewer.
  diff=$(awk -v a="$total" -v b="$ofin" 'function ab(x) { return x < 0 ? -x : x } BEGIN { if (b > 0) printf "%.1f", 100 * ab(a - b) / b; else print "null" }')
  idiff=$(awk -v a="$inv" -v b="$handled" 'function ab(x) { return x < 0 ? -x : x } BEGIN { if (b > 0) printf "%.1f", 100 * ab(a - b) / b; else print "null" }')
  echo "$run: Splunk's orders count differs from orders' own log by $diff%; inventory's by $idiff%"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_orders_error_pct_after[$run]=$pct"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_log_diff_pct[$run]=$diff"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_inventory_diff_pct[$run]=$idiff"
  # The retry storm as Splunk sees it: calls orders made to inventory (its HTTP client metric) per order request
  cpo=$(awk -v c="$calls" -v t="$total" 'BEGIN { if (t > 0) printf "%.2f", c / t; else print "null" }')
  echo "$run: in Splunk, orders made $calls calls to inventory for $total order requests ($cpo per order); orders' log: $ocalls for $ofin"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_inventory_calls_per_order[$run]=$cpo"
  [ "$run" = budget-2 ] && splunk_total=$total
done
echo "-- the service map in Splunk APM for this environment"
show_map <<<"$(topology)"

# The gate: every budget run started healthy (report checks that) and recovered inside its window, and Splunk returned
# the budget-2 window. Whether a naive run recovers is a result, not a gate.
all=1
for run in budget-1 budget-2 budget-3; do
  r=$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: recovery_after_slowdown\[$run\/recovered\]=//p" "report-$run.txt" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$run recovered within the window: ${r:-unknown}"
  [ "${r:-0}" = 1 ] || all=0
done
if [ "$all" = 1 ] && [ "${splunk_total:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
  emit fixed
else
  emit not_fixed
fi

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-src
  namespace: demo
data:
  requirements.txt: |
    flask==3.1.3
    waitress==3.0.2
    requests==2.34.2
    opentelemetry-distro==0.66b2
    opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.45.2
    opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask==0.66b2
    opentelemetry-instrumentation-requests==0.66b2

  inventory.py: |
    # inventory: reserves stock. A fixed pool of sync workers, each request holds one for WORK_MS. During a brownout every
    # request takes BROWNOUT_MS instead, as if a dependency were stuck. Requests a client already gave up on are still worked,
    # because a sync worker can't tell, which is what makes a backlog expensive.
    import os, threading, time
    from flask import Flask, request
    app = Flask(__name__)
    WORK_MS = int(os.environ.get("WORK_MS", "40"))
    STATE = os.environ.get("BROWNOUT_FILE", "/tmp/brownout")    # shared by every worker process
    stats = {"handled": 0, "late": 0}
    lock = threading.Lock()

    @app.post("/admin/brownout")
    def brownout():
        secs, delay = float(request.args.get("seconds", "30")), int(request.args.get("delay_ms", "2000"))
        until = time.time() + secs
        with open(STATE, "w") as f:
            f.write(f"{until} {delay}")
        print(f"BROWNOUT start seconds={secs:g} delay_ms={delay} until={until:.0f}", flush=True)
        return {"until": until}

    def current_delay():
        try:
            until, delay = open(STATE).read().split()
            return int(delay) if time.time() < float(until) else WORK_MS
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            return WORK_MS

    @app.get("/reserve/<int:order>")
    def reserve(order):
        # orders sends the moment its own timeout runs out. Starting after that means nobody is waiting for this answer.
        deadline = float(request.headers.get("X-Caller-Deadline", "0") or 0)
        late = deadline > 0 and time.time() > deadline
        time.sleep(current_delay() / 1000)
        with lock:
            stats["handled"] += 1
            stats["late"] += late
        return {"order": order, "reserved": True}

    SERVER = {}   # the running waitress server, so the reporter can read its queue

    def node_cpu():
        # /proc/stat isn't namespaced, so this is the whole node: busy and total jiffies across all CPUs
        f = [int(x) for x in open("/proc/stat").readline().split()[1:]]
        return sum(f) - f[3] - f[4], sum(f)

    def reporter():
        # One line a second: requests finished and started late in that second, requests accepted but waiting for a thread,
        # this container's CPU time so far (cgroup) and the node's CPU counters. Single process, so this is the whole service.
        last, last_late = 0, 0
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
            with lock:
                now, late = stats["handled"], stats["late"]
            try:
                cpu = next(l.split()[1] for l in open("/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat") if l.startswith("usage_usec"))
            except (OSError, StopIteration):
                cpu = "na"
            busy, total = node_cpu()
            q = len(SERVER["s"].task_dispatcher.queue) if "s" in SERVER else -1
            print(f"INVENTORY t={int(time.time())} handled={now - last} late={late - last_late} queued={q} cpu_usec={cpu} node_busy={busy} node_total={total}", flush=True)
            last, last_late = now, late

    threading.Thread(target=reporter, daemon=True).start()

    @app.get("/healthz")
    def healthz():
        return "ok"

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        # waitress: one process, a fixed pool of worker threads and a queue in front of them. No fork, so zero-code
        # OpenTelemetry works unchanged.
        import logging
        from waitress import serve
        logging.getLogger("waitress.queue").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
        from waitress.server import create_server
        s = create_server(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8081")), threads=int(os.environ.get("THREADS", "4")),
                          connection_limit=900, backlog=2048, channel_timeout=120)
        SERVER["s"] = s
        a = s.adj
        print(f"INVENTORY server threads={a.threads} backlog={a.backlog} connection_limit={a.connection_limit} work_ms={WORK_MS}", flush=True)
        s.run()

  orders.py: |
    # orders: takes an order and reserves it in inventory with a 500 ms timeout. RETRY_MODE decides what happens on a failure:
    #   naive  - retry at once, up to RETRIES more times
    #   budget - retry with exponential backoff and full jitter, and only while the retry budget allows: each order adds
    #            BUDGET_RATIO of a token, each retry spends one, so retries stay a small share of traffic
    import os, random, threading, time
    import requests
    from flask import Flask
    app = Flask(__name__)
    INVENTORY = os.environ.get("INVENTORY_URL", "http://localhost:8081")
    MODE = os.environ.get("RETRY_MODE", "naive")
    RETRIES = int(os.environ.get("RETRIES", "3"))
    TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("TIMEOUT_S", "0.5"))
    BASE, CAP = float(os.environ.get("BACKOFF_BASE_S", "0.1")), float(os.environ.get("BACKOFF_CAP_S", "2"))
    RATIO, MAX_TOKENS = float(os.environ.get("BUDGET_RATIO", "0.1")), float(os.environ.get("BUDGET_MAX", "10"))
    tokens, lock = [MAX_TOKENS], threading.Lock()
    errs = {"timeout": 0, "conn": 0, "http": 0}   # failed calls by kind, reported each second
    session = requests.Session()
    session.mount("http://", requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=4, pool_maxsize=256))

    def may_retry():
        if MODE != "budget":
            return True
        with lock:
            if tokens[0] >= 1:
                tokens[0] -= 1
                return True
            return False

    import logging
    log = logging.getLogger("orders"); logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")

    @app.post("/orders/<int:order>")
    def place(order):
        began = time.time()
        ok, attempts, denied = reserve_with_retries(order)
        log.info("ORDER %d ok=%d attempts=%d denied=%d ms=%d t=%d", order, ok, attempts, denied, (time.time() - began) * 1000, int(began))
        return ({"order": order, "attempts": attempts}, 200) if ok else ({"order": order, "failed": True}, 503)

    def reserve_with_retries(order):
        if MODE == "budget":
            with lock:
                tokens[0] = min(MAX_TOKENS, tokens[0] + RATIO)
        for attempt in range(RETRIES + 1):
            try:
                r = session.get(f"{INVENTORY}/reserve/{order}", timeout=TIMEOUT, headers={"X-Caller-Deadline": f"{time.time() + TIMEOUT:.3f}"})
                if r.status_code == 200:
                    return True, attempt + 1, 0
                kind = "http"
            except requests.Timeout:
                kind = "timeout"
            except requests.RequestException:
                kind = "conn"   # refused or reset, not a timeout
            with lock:
                errs[kind] += 1
            if attempt == RETRIES:
                break
            if not may_retry():
                return False, attempt + 1, 1   # the budget was spent, so this order fails without a retry
            if MODE == "budget":
                time.sleep(random.uniform(0, min(CAP, BASE * 2 ** attempt)))
        return False, attempt + 1, 0

    def reporter():
        # One line a second with this container's CPU time so far, from its cgroup, so a busy orders pod would show.
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
            try:
                cpu = next(l.split()[1] for l in open("/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat") if l.startswith("usage_usec"))
            except (OSError, StopIteration):
                cpu = "na"
            with lock:
                e = dict(errs); errs.update(timeout=0, conn=0, http=0)
            print(f"ORDERS t={int(time.time())} cpu_usec={cpu} timeouts={e['timeout']} conn_errors={e['conn']} http_errors={e['http']}", flush=True)

    threading.Thread(target=reporter, daemon=True).start()

    @app.get("/healthz")
    def healthz():
        return "ok"

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        import logging
        from waitress import serve
        logging.getLogger("waitress.queue").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
        serve(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8080")), threads=int(os.environ.get("THREADS", "400")),
              connection_limit=900, backlog=2048, channel_timeout=120)

# Builds one virtualenv on the app node with pinned packages, once. Both services run from it, in every run.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: build
  namespace: demo
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 420
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeName: APP_NODE
      volumes:
        - name: src
          configMap:
            name: app-src
        - name: lab
          hostPath:
            path: /opt/lab
            type: DirectoryOrCreate
      containers:
        - name: build
          image: python:3.12-slim
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: src, mountPath: /src, readOnly: true }
            - { name: lab, mountPath: /lab }
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              set -e
              rm -rf /lab/venv /lab/app && mkdir -p /lab/app
              cp /src/inventory.py /src/orders.py /src/requirements.txt /lab/app/
              python -m venv /lab/venv
              for i in 1 2 3; do /lab/venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir -r /lab/app/requirements.txt && break; echo "pip attempt $i failed"; sleep 10; done
              /lab/venv/bin/pip freeze | grep -iE '^(flask|waitress|requests|opentelemetry-(distro|sdk|exporter-otlp-proto-http|instrumentation-flask|instrumentation-requests))=='
              sha256sum /lab/app/*.py

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Open-loop load: RATE orders a second whatever happens, as real users keep arriving. At SLOW_AT seconds it asks
    # inventory for a slowdown of SLOW_SECONDS, then keeps sending. Prints one line per second, with epoch times.
    import os, threading, time, http.client
    RATE, SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("RATE", "60")), int(os.environ.get("LOAD_SECONDS", "170"))
    HOST, PORT = os.environ.get("ORDERS_HOST", "localhost"), int(os.environ.get("ORDERS_PORT", "8080"))
    INV, INV_PORT = os.environ.get("INVENTORY_HOST", "localhost"), int(os.environ.get("INVENTORY_PORT", "8081"))
    FIRST = int(os.environ.get("FIRST", "1"))
    SLOW_AT, SLOW_S, SLOW_MS = int(os.environ.get("SLOW_AT", "30")), int(os.environ.get("SLOW_SECONDS", "20")), int(os.environ.get("SLOW_MS", "2000"))
    res, lock = {}, threading.Lock()

    def one(n, sec):
        ok = False
        try:
            c = http.client.HTTPConnection(HOST, PORT, timeout=5)
            c.request("POST", f"/orders/{n}")
            ok = c.getresponse().status == 200
            c.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        with lock:
            res.setdefault(sec, [0, 0])[0 if ok else 1] += 1

    def slowdown():
        c = http.client.HTTPConnection(INV, INV_PORT, timeout=10)
        c.request("POST", f"/admin/brownout?seconds={SLOW_S}&delay_ms={SLOW_MS}")
        print("SLOWDOWN reply", c.getresponse().status, flush=True)

    t0 = time.time(); n = FIRST
    print(f"LOAD start={t0:.0f} rate={RATE} seconds={SECONDS} first={FIRST}", flush=True)
    for sec in range(SECONDS):
        if sec == SLOW_AT:
            print(f"SLOWDOWN start={time.time():.0f} end={time.time() + SLOW_S:.0f} second={SLOW_AT} seconds={SLOW_S} delay_ms={SLOW_MS}", flush=True)
            threading.Thread(target=slowdown, daemon=True).start()
        for i in range(RATE):
            threading.Thread(target=one, args=(n, sec), daemon=True).start(); n += 1
            time.sleep(max(0, t0 + sec + (i + 1) / RATE - time.time()))
    time.sleep(6)
    for sec in range(SECONDS):
        ok, bad = res.get(sec, [0, 0])
        print(f"LOAD second={sec} ok={ok} failed={bad}")
    print(f"LOAD end={time.time():.0f} sent={n - FIRST} ok={sum(v[0] for v in res.values())} failed={sum(v[1] for v in res.values())}")

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: LOAD_NODE
  enableServiceLinks: false   # Kubernetes would otherwise set ORDERS_PORT=tcp://..., which load.py reads as a port
  volumes:
    - name: load
      configMap:
        name: load
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "/load/load.py"]
      env:
        - { name: RATE, value: "40" }
        - { name: LOAD_SECONDS, value: "110" }
        - { name: FIRST, value: "FIRST" }
        - { name: ORDERS_HOST, value: "orders" }
        - { name: INVENTORY_HOST, value: "inventory" }
        - { name: SLOW_AT, value: "20" }
        - { name: SLOW_SECONDS, value: "20" }
        - { name: SLOW_MS, value: "2000" }
      volumeMounts:
        - { name: load, mountPath: /load }
      resources:
        requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi }

# Shared by reproduce.sh and fix.sh: the clock, starting a run, the load and the per-run report. Sourced, never run alone.
# One run = fresh orders and inventory pods with one RETRY_MODE, 110 s of open-loop load at 40 orders a second, and a
# 20 s inventory slowdown at second 20 that the load pod itself asks for. analyze.sh turns the three logs into counts.
# Runs alternate: naive-1, budget-1 and naive-2 in reproduce.sh, then budget-2, naive-3 and budget-3 in fix.sh.
export LC_ALL=C

start_clock() {   # seconds allowed, the result to print on failure. Every wait is capped so a result always prints.
  START=$(date +%s); LIMIT=$1; FAILED=$2; HERO_DONE=0
  trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $FAILED"; }' EXIT
}
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit "$FAILED"; exit 0; }

newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }
why() { kubectl -n demo get pods -o wide | tail -6; kubectl -n demo get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -8 | cut -c1-180; kubectl -n demo logs deploy/"$1" --tail=20 | cut -c1-200; }

# Each run has its own order numbers, so no log can mix runs: naive-1 from 1, budget-1 from 10001, naive-2 from 20001...
first_order() { case "$1" in naive-1) echo 1 ;; budget-1) echo 10001 ;; naive-2) echo 20001 ;; budget-2) echo 30001 ;; naive-3) echo 40001 ;; budget-3) echo 50001 ;; esac; }

# Fresh pods for both services with one retry mode, then proof of what each pod really runs.
start_run() {   # run label (naive-1, budget-2, ...), seconds allowed
  local mode=${1%-*}
  kubectl -n demo set env deployment/orders "RETRY_MODE=$mode" "LAB_RUN=$1" >/dev/null || fail "could not set orders"
  kubectl -n demo set env deployment/inventory "LAB_RUN=$1" >/dev/null || fail "could not set inventory"
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why inventory; fail "inventory did not roll out"; }
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why orders; fail "orders did not roll out"; }
  local i o
  i=$(newest inventory); o=$(newest orders)
  [ "$(kubectl -n demo exec "$o" -- printenv RETRY_MODE)" = "$mode" ] || fail "orders is not in $mode mode"
  echo "$1: ${i#pod/} and ${o#pod/}, RETRY_MODE=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$o" -- printenv RETRY_MODE), environment $(kubectl -n demo exec "$o" -- printenv OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES | sed 's/,.*//; s/.*=//'), app $(kubectl -n demo exec "$i" -- sha256sum /lab/app/inventory.py | cut -c1-12) $(kubectl -n demo exec "$o" -- sha256sum /lab/app/orders.py | cut -c1-12)"
  if [ "$1" = naive-1 ]; then   # the same in every run, so printed once
    echo "image $(kubectl -n demo get "$i" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}'); inventory THREADS=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$i" -- printenv THREADS) WORK_MS=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$i" -- printenv WORK_MS); orders THREADS=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$o" -- printenv THREADS)"
    echo "orders retry settings: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$o" -- sh -c 'grep -E "^(RETRIES|TIMEOUT|BASE, CAP|RATIO, MAX_TOKENS) " /lab/app/orders.py' | sed -E 's/(int|float)\(os\.environ\.get\(//g; s/\)\)//g' | tr -s ' ' | tr '\n' ';' | cut -c1-300)"
    echo "inventory as it runs: $(kubectl -n demo logs "$i" | grep -m1 'INVENTORY server' || echo 'line missing'); node somaxconn $(kubectl -n demo exec "$i" -- cat /proc/sys/net/core/somaxconn); CPU limits: '$(kubectl -n demo get pods -l 'app in (orders,inventory)' -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[0].resources.limits.cpu}{end}')' (empty means none)"
  fi
}

# The load pod sends 40 orders a second for 110 s and asks inventory for the slowdown at second 20.
load_run() {   # run label, seconds allowed
  kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
  sed -e "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" -e "s/value: \"FIRST\"/value: \"$(first_order "$1")\"/" k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$2s" >/dev/null || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=20; why orders; fail "the load did not finish"; }
  kubectl -n demo logs load > "load-$1.txt"
  kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest orders)" > "orders-$1.log" 2>/dev/null
  kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest inventory)" > "inventory-$1.log" 2>/dev/null
  grep -E '^(LOAD start|SLOWDOWN start|LOAD end)' "load-$1.txt" | tr '\n' ' '; echo
}

# The lab's runner has no Python, so analyze.sh runs in a small python:3.12-slim pod on the load node, on copies of the logs.
analyzer() {
  kubectl -n demo get pod analyzer >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
  kubectl -n demo run analyzer --image=python:3.12-slim --restart=Never \
    --overrides="{\"spec\":{\"nodeName\":\"$LOAD_NODE\",\"enableServiceLinks\":false}}" -- sleep 86400 >/dev/null || fail "could not start the analyzer pod"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/analyzer --for=condition=Ready --timeout=120s >/dev/null || fail "the analyzer pod did not start"
}

report() {   # run label. Sets before_pct, recovered and failed_after from analyze.sh's output.
  analyzer
  local f
  kubectl -n demo exec analyzer -- mkdir -p /work >/dev/null
  for f in analyze.sh "load-$1.txt" "orders-$1.log" "inventory-$1.log"; do kubectl -n demo cp "$f" "analyzer:/work/$f" >/dev/null || fail "could not copy $f"; done
  kubectl -n demo exec analyzer -- bash /work/analyze.sh "$1" "/work/load-$1.txt" "/work/orders-$1.log" "/work/inventory-$1.log" | tee "report-$1.txt"
  sed -n "s/^WINDOW $1 //p" "report-$1.txt" > "window-$1.txt"
  before_pct=$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: orders_success_before_pct\[$1\]=//p" "report-$1.txt")
  recovered=$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: recovery_after_slowdown\[$1\/recovered\]=//p" "report-$1.txt")
  failed_after=$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: failed_orders_after_slowdown\[$1\]=//p" "report-$1.txt")
  awk -v p="${before_pct:-0}" 'BEGIN { exit !(p >= 95) }' || fail "the $1 run started unhealthy: ${before_pct:-no} % success before the slowdown"
  # The positive control for the slowdown itself: if no order failed during it, a recovery would prove nothing.
  [ "$(sed -n "s/^HERO_MEASURE: failed_orders_during_slowdown\[$1\]=//p" "report-$1.txt")" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null || fail "no order failed during the $1 slowdown, so it had no effect"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: instant retries. orders calls inventory with a 500 ms timeout and retries a failed call at once, up to 3 more
# times. Open-loop load of 40 orders a second; at second 20 inventory slows to 2 s a request for 20 s, then is healthy.
# Sets up the cluster, then runs naive-1, budget-1 and naive-2. fix.sh runs budget-2, naive-3 and budget-3.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh

start_clock 810 not_reproduced

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,TYPE:.metadata.labels.node\.kubernetes\.io/instance-type,READY:.status.conditions[-1].type || true
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 500)s" >/dev/null || true

# The services stay on one node and the load on the other, in both runs.
APP_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
LOAD_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$APP_NODE" > app-node.txt
echo "$LOAD_NODE" > load-node.txt
echo "app node: $APP_NODE; load node: $LOAD_NODE"

[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] && [ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "the Splunk settings are not set"

echo "== 2. Installing the Splunk OTel Collector (chart 0.163.1), the same in both runs"
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1
helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector \
  --version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace \
  --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws \
  --set distribution=eks \
  >/dev/null || fail "collector install failed"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 150 500)s" >/dev/null || fail "collector agent not ready"
echo "collector agent ready on $(kubectl -n splunk get daemonset splunk-otel-collector-agent -o jsonpath='{.status.numberReady}') nodes"

echo "== 3. Building one virtualenv with pinned packages on the app node"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the build"
state=""
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 360 330)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  state=$(kubectl -n demo get job build -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$state" in *Complete*|*Failed*) break ;; esac
  sleep 10
done
kubectl -n demo logs job/build --tail=10 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^\[notice\]' | cut -c1-300 | tail -3 || true
case "$state" in *Complete*) ;; *) kubectl -n demo describe job build | tail -15; fail "the build did not finish: ${state:-still running}" ;; esac
echo "build took $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

echo "== 4. Deploying inventory and orders with zero-code OpenTelemetry"
sed -e "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" -e "s/LAB_ENV/$LAB_NAME/g" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy the services"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 290)s" >/dev/null || { why inventory; fail "inventory did not start"; }

# Splunk Observability Cloud reads for fix.sh: request counts from the services' HTTP metrics, and the APM service map. Sourced, never run alone. Needs SPLUNK_REALM and SPLUNK_API_TOKEN.
# Every SignalFlow program sent is printed, and its points are summed over one window.
API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
STREAM="https://stream.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
series() { curl -sS --max-time 20 -G -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/metrictimeseries" --data-urlencode "query=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=1000" 2>/dev/null; }

wait_cluster() {   # seconds. Sets cluster to how many of the cluster's series Splunk holds.
  local t0=$(date +%s); cluster=0
  while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$1" ]; do
    cluster=$(series "k8s.cluster.name:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.count // (.results | length) // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    [ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
    sleep 15
  done
}

# SignalFlow answers as a stream of events. This prints one value per point between start and stop, summed across series.
signalflow() {   # program, start ms, stop ms, resolution ms
  curl -sS --max-time 60 -X POST -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" --data-binary "$1" \
    "$STREAM/v2/signalflow/execute?start=$2&stop=$3&resolution=${4:-10000}&immediate=true" 2>/dev/null |
    awk '/^event:/ { if (b != "") print e "\t" b; e = $2; b = ""; next }
         /^data:/  { sub(/^data: ?/, ""); b = b $0; next }
         END       { if (b != "") print e "\t" b }' |
    jq -Rr --argjson from "$2" --argjson to "$3" 'split("\t") | select(.[0] == "data") | (.[1] | fromjson? // {})
      | select(.logicalTimestampMs >= $from and .logicalTimestampMs < $to) | "\(.logicalTimestampMs) \([.data[]?.value // empty] | add // 0)"' 2>/dev/null
}

# Reads the same count until two reads in a row agree, so a count isn't taken before Splunk has all of it. Sets count.
stable_count() {   # service, errors: all|true, start s, stop s
  local prev="" try
  for try in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
    count=$(apm_count "$@")
    if [ -n "$prev" ] && [ "$count" = "$prev" ] && { [ "$count" != 0 ] || [ "$2" = true ]; }; then   # zero errors twice is a real zero
      echo "  $1 $2 $3-$4 per 10 s: $(awk '{printf "%s ", $2}' "sf-$1-$2.txt")= $count (read $try times)" >&2
      return 0
    fi
    prev=$count; sleep 15
  done
  echo "  $1 $2 $3-$4 per 10 s: $(awk '{printf "%s ", $2}' "sf-$1-$2.txt")= $count (reads didn't settle)" >&2
}

# The service map Splunk APM builds for this lab's environment over the last 25 minutes.
topology() {
  local now=$(date +%s) body
  body=$(jq -cn --arg t "$(( (now - 1500) * 1000 ))/$(( now * 1000 ))" --arg e "$LAB_NAME" '{timeRange: $t, tagFilters: [{name: "sf_environment", operator: "equals", scope: "GLOBAL", value: $e}]}')
  curl -sS --max-time 20 -X POST -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$body" "$API/v2/apm/topology" 2>/dev/null
}
show_map() { jq -r '(.data.nodes[]? | "  \(.serviceName) inferred=\(.inferred // false)"), (.data.edges[]? | "  \(.fromNode) -> \(.toNode)")' 2>/dev/null || true; }

# Request counts for one service's route in one window, from the stable HTTP server metric the services send through the
# Collector (http.server.request.duration, so Splunk stores http.server.request.duration_count). Readiness probes hit
# /healthz, so filtering on the route keeps them out. Prints the per-10 s points to stderr.
route_of() { case "$1" in orders) echo '/orders/<int:order>' ;; inventory) echo '/reserve/<int:order>' ;; esac; }
apm_count() {   # service, errors: all|true|client, start s, stop s
  local f="filter('deployment.environment', '$LAB_NAME') and filter('service.name', '$1') and filter('http.route', '$(route_of "$1")')" try n m=http.server.request.duration_count
  [ "$2" = true ] && f="$f and filter('http.response.status_code', '503')"
  # client: every call orders made to inventory, timeouts included, from orders' own HTTP client metric
  [ "$2" = client ] && { m=http.client.request.duration_count; f="filter('deployment.environment', '$LAB_NAME') and filter('service.name', '$1') and filter('server.address', 'inventory')"; }
  local prog="data('$m', filter=$f, rollup='delta').sum().publish()"
  [ -e "prog-$1-$2.seen" ] || { echo "  program: $prog" >&2; : > "prog-$1-$2.seen"; }   # once per read (apm_count runs in a subshell)
  for try in 1 2 3; do   # a stream can come back empty once, so an empty read is asked again
    signalflow "$prog" "$(( $3 * 1000 ))" "$(( $4 * 1000 ))" > "sf-$1-$2.txt"
    n=$(awk '{t += $2} END {printf "%.0f", t}' "sf-$1-$2.txt")
    [ -s "sf-$1-$2.txt" ] && break
    echo "  read $try came back empty; reading again" >&2; sleep 10
  done
  if [ "${n:-0}" = 0 ] && [ "$2" = all ]; then   # say what Splunk does hold for this service, so a wrong name or label shows
    series "sf_metric:http.* AND deployment.environment:$LAB_NAME AND service.name:$1" | jq -r '.results[:6][]? | "  held: \(.metric) \(.dimensions | to_entries | map("\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(" "))"' >&2
  fi
  echo "${n:-0}"
}
